title: HOW ZERODHA BUILT A PROFITABLE BROKERAGE WITHOUT VENTURE CAPITAL
text:
A stock broker that has never taken venture money still reported a net profit of Rs 4,237 crore for FY25. Zerodha, started in 2010, is that broker, and its growth came from its own customers.
Zerodha is a discount stock broker run by brothers Nithin and Nikhil Kamath. It charges nothing for equity delivery trades and a flat fee on most other trades. Brokerage is its main income, with smaller amounts from other fees and interest.
Many brokers took a cut on every trade. Zerodha went the other way, using flat-fee pricing instead of high commissions. Its 2015 pricing set delivery trades at zero,…
company: Zerodha (founded by Nithin and Nikhil Kamath)

title: HOW SEVEN MUMBAI WOMEN TURNED RS 80 INTO A PAPAD COOPERATIVE WORTH MILLIONS
text:
Seven women in Mumbai started a papad business in 1959 with a sum of just Rs 80. Their cooperative now reports more than $200 million in sales.
Lijjat makes papads, masalas, wheat flour, chapatis and detergent, and sells them in India and abroad. It is a cooperative, so each member is a co-owner and profits are shared equally.
Lijjat has no single owner. Women roll papad from home through local branches, and any woman who wants to join can approach one. The papad is kept to one standard, and quality is never compromised.
Open membership and fixed quality kept it growing. It employs more than…
company: Shri Mahila Griha Udyog Lijjat Papad

title: HOW AMUL'S FARMER-POOLED CO-OP TURNED MILK INTO A RS 1 LAKH CRORE BRAND
text:
A dairy brand built by 36 lakh farmers pushed its turnover past Rs 1 lakh crore in FY 2025-26. That was an 11% rise on a Rs 90,000 crore base the year before.
Amul runs as three layers. Village societies collect milk, district unions process and test it, and a state federation markets the finished products under the Amul name. It also makes dairy goods for other brands.
Rather than dealing with each farmer one by one, Amul groups small milk producers into village-level societies. Much of the money shoppers pay is sent back to those farmers.

Why Ashok Leyland’s investors are wary despite robust demand
text: Ashok Leyland's margins have been strained by industry-wide cost pressures, even as demand holds strong despite a high base.

title: SBI trades firm in down market, stock up 16% in Nov; brokerages stay upbeat
text: SBI's share price hit intraday high of ₹1,118.55, trading at its highest level since August 7, 2026 and 10% away from its record high of ₹1,234.80 hit on February 24, 2026.

title: China and India mask a growing crisis in global coal
text: Global coal consumption is resilient due to rising demand from China and India, which is increasing despite declining figures elsewhere. However, many coal exporters are struggling financially as they face significant losses in their operations. The coal industry is experiencing tough economic conditions, with job losses and company closures becoming commonplace.

title: Nepal gets nod to import 350 MW of power from India during winter
text: Nepal has gained authorization to import up to 350 MW of electricity from India amid declining hydropower generation. This approval will remain effective from November 17, 2026, until July 31, 2027. The Nepal Electricity Authority can procure electricity through various transmission lines to meet domestic demand. Several hydropower projects have been affected by recent floods, limiting local production capabilities.

title: Adani Airport Holdings unveils next-generation Adani Rewards membership across eight airports
text: Adani Airport Holdings has launched an upgraded rewards membership programme across eight airports, offering passengers benefits worth up to Rs 65,000 annually. Integrated with Adani OneApp, the tier-based scheme combines travel, shopping, dining and lounge privileges as the company looks to boost digital transactions and non-aeronautical revenue.

title: Mukesh Ambani seeks to build satellite capacity for Starlink challenge
text: Reliance Group is eyeing partnerships for manufacturing a 1,600-satellite broadband network aimed at competing with Starlink. The planned low-earth orbit constellation aims for completion by 2035 to enhance connectivity in India. Reliance is negotiating with both domestic and international manufacturers to support its manufacturing goals.

title: What are India's leading enterprises learning from their AI deployments?
text: Indian enterprises are moving AI into financial services, retail, supply chains and manufacturing. Survey findings show growing adoption and measurable returns, but data readiness, compliance and organisational change remain significant challenges.

title: ONGC gas leak in Andhra Pradesh's Konaseema forces evacuation of around 800 people
text: A gas leak occurred at an ONGC gas well in Geddada, prompting the evacuation of around 800 residents. Authorities cordoned off a 1 km radius around the well and diverted traffic along National Highway 216. Local officials instructed residents to avoid electrical appliances and gas stoves to prevent ignition. Continuous monitoring revealed zero gas concentration at the assessed locations after the leak began.

title: Porsche India inaugurates its largest after-sales facility in Kolkata
text: Spanning more than 32,000 square feet, the state-of-the-art facility has been designed in accordance with Porsche's latest global Corporate Identity standards, the luxury automaker said.

title: India backs fair trade but won't allow unfairly priced imports to hurt steel sector: ISA
text: Naveen Jindal, President of the Indian Steel Association, highlighted the importance of fair trade for the steel industry. He noted that India's steel sector can expand significantly by 2030-31 if challenges are addressed. Jindal emphasized embracing technology, particularly artificial intelligence, to improve operations and sustainability. Concerns were raised regarding Chinese steel exports and trade barriers posed by developed economies.

title: VB-GRAMG may cost states up to six times more than MGNREGA: Report
text: The new rural employment scheme VB-GRAMG was estimated to cost states six times more than MGNREGA. Larger states like Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Uttar Pradesh would face additional expenditures of Rs 2,000-3,000 crore. The Centre and states would share costs under VB-GRAMG, raising state financial burdens significantly. A state's share would depend on the 16th Finance Commission's devolution parameters.

title: Govt says Xiaomi, Flextronics hid royalty deals in tariff fight
text: The Indian government has accused Xiaomi India and contract manufacturer Flex of failing to fully disclose royalty arrangements, as it seeks to recover unpaid customs duties and penalties. The dispute could cost Xiaomi more than $150 million and centres on whether royalty payments to technology partners should be included in the value of imported smartphone components. The Supreme Court is hearing Xiaomi's challenge.

title: BMW bets on luxury Alpina brand to woo wealthy Indian buyers in challenge to Mercedes
text: The German carmaker will roll out Alpina as a "standalone brand" across 10 Indian cities and has started recruiting candidates for a network strategy role that includes selecting dealer partners, analysing competition and planning a rollout, according to a job posting on LinkedIn.

title: Indian technology companies widen their European footprint, from services to strategy
text: Indian technology companies are broadening their European presence beyond traditional IT services, with Paris Region emerging as a strategic hub: 30% of France’s GDP, a dense research ecosystem anchored by Paris-Saclay and 89 Indian companies already established. Choose Paris Region, which has a permanent office in Mumbai, leading a delegation to the Bengaluru Tech Summit (17-19 November) to deepen this India-Europe strategic corridor.

title: Reliance plans to invest about $1.6 billion to build new biogas plants
text: Reliance Industries is set to invest about Rs 15,000 crore in the establishment of nearly 100 compressed biogas plants in India by 2030. With 45 biogas plants already in operation, Reliance plans a substantial increase by March 2027 to further support the nation's energy mix goals.

title: UPI and the trust pact in its second act
text: As tap-and-pay, UPI AutoPay mandates and agentic commerce take hold, more payments in India will go through without a customer entering a PIN or approving each transaction. At a closed-door roundtable hosted by Mindgate Solutions with PayU, industry leaders examined what that shift demands of payment providers and merchants, and who pays for it. Read on for the trends to watch.

title: India, other major APAC nations to maintain strong prudential oversight: Moody's
text: Moody's Ratings suggests that key Asia-Pacific countries are set to uphold strong prudential supervision, which acts as a bulwark against excessive risk-taking and reinforces banks' capital buffers. This stability projects a positive outlook for global banks in 2027, supported by resilient macroeconomic conditions that exhibit their adaptability in adverse circumstances. The upcoming year will see six defining themes influencing bank credit quality.

title: UPI’s free era is ending. Who pays, who earns, and who gets left behind?
text: A slice of UPI is likely to stop being free in the future. At a closed-door roundtable in Bengaluru, the people who build, lend and collect on India’s favourite payments rail debated what this means for merchants, TPAPs and the economics of the ecosystem. Read on for the sharp insights.

title: Air India, Airbus to develop voluntary corporate SAF programme
text: Air India and Airbus are collaborating to develop a voluntary Sustainable Aviation Fuel programme for the aviation sector. The feasibility study will explore methods to reduce emissions linked to air travel. The Indian government plans to mandate a 1 percent blending of SAF in jet fuel by 2027. Investments of USD 70-85 billion are anticipated to support SAF production by 2040.

title: Anil Agarwal warns ONGC's takeover of Vedanta's oilfield risks denting investor confidence
text: Vedanta chairman Anil Agarwal has warned that the transfer of its producing Cambay offshore oil and gas block to ONGC could send the wrong signal to investors. Urging regulatory stability, Agarwal said Vedanta was committing $5 billion to boost oil and gas production. He called on the government to avoid disrupting existing operators as India seeks to cut energy imports.

title: JSW Steel CEO flags Chinese exports, trade barriers as key challenges
text: JSW Steel's CEO Jayant Acharya highlighted the impact of Chinese steel exports on Indian steelmakers. He stated that tariff and non-tariff barriers in developed markets complicate the situation. Despite these challenges, domestic steel demand in India remains strong. Acharya emphasized the need for India to open more iron ore mines for adequate raw material supply. This initiative would support the future growth of the steel industry.

title: DRI searches Cipla's Mumbai office, Bhiwandi depot over imported drugs
text: The Directorate of Revenue Intelligence's Mumbai zonal unit has searched Cipla's office in Vikhroli and its depot in Bhiwandi over the classification or exemption of an imported pharmaceutical finished product. Cipla said it cooperated with authorities and that the proceedings would have no material impact on its financials or operations.

title: Tata Steel seeks UK market support, Dutch green funds amid Chinese excessive supply: Narendran
text: Tata Steel is seeking UK government intervention to address excess steel inventories and negotiating Dutch state funding for its green transition as Chinese oversupply, geopolitical conflicts and trade barriers disrupt global markets. CEO T V Narendran says the company is prioritising cost efficiency, value-added products and cleaner steelmaking to build resilience.

title: SAF policy draft to be out in 2 weeks as India eyes $85 billion aviation fuel opportunity
text: The government of India plans to release the draft sustainable aviation fuel policy for public commentary soon. This initiative aims to enhance local production and reduce the country's reliance on fuel imports. Approximately 10 million tonnes of sustainable aviation fuel could be produced annually by 2040. The policy will support only indigenously manufactured fuel to blend with Aviation Turbine Fuel.

title: IL&FS crisis was India's Lehman moment, swift action helped contain contagion: Uday Kotak
text: Uday Kotak has described the 2018 IL&FS crisis as India's Lehman Brothers moment, warning that the collapse could have triggered widespread contagion across the financial sector. He credited swift government intervention and coordination with regulators and stakeholders for containing the crisis. IL&FS had 340 companies and defaulted on over Rs 91,000 crore despite holding a triple-A rating.

title: Midterm Meltdown: How US elections sparked a rethink on energy risks
text: Energy markets from crude oil and diesel to natural gas, LNG, coal and tanker freight have declined since the US midterm elections, suggesting traders are pricing in a lower risk of wider conflict in the Middle East. However, Europe's low gas inventories and potential supply disruptions remain significant risks.

title: ONGC gas leak in Andhra's Konaseema forces evacuation of around 800 people
text: A gas leak at an ONGC well in Geddada village in Andhra Pradesh's Dr BR Ambedkar Konaseema district on Tuesday prompted the evacuation of nearly 800 people living within a 1-km radius. The leak began during workover operations around 5 am, with authorities deploying a water blanket to contain it.

title: Decoding vitamin deficiency and hair fall:  Signs, tests and next steps
text: If you're dealing with hair loss, it might be linked to overlooked nutritional deficiencies. Key vitamins and minerals, like vitamin D, iron, and B12, are vital for optimal hair health. Symptoms such as tiredness, dry hair, or breakage can signal these deficiencies. To diagnose accurately, a blood test is crucial, and seeking professional guidance can help tailor a treatment plan to prevent further hair loss.

title: Tata Steel eyes 50 MT capacity in India, to pump 75% of capex into domestic growth: TV Narendran
text: Tata Steel is planning to increase its steelmaking capacity in India to 50 million tonnes by exploring new projects. The company aims to establish a 15 million tonne greenfield plant in Maharashtra to facilitate growth. Investment plans include spending approximately Rs 18,000-20,000 crore this year, predominantly in India.

title: Japan proposes Asia oil security task force at ASEAN summit
text: Japan has proposed a task force to enhance oil stockpiling cooperation among Asian countries during emergencies. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi emphasized coordination with a Philippine-led oil stockpiling initiative. The proposal is in response to vulnerabilities exposed by recent conflicts affecting oil supplies. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. highlighted the importance of sustainable energy security and regional cooperation.

title: India facing aircraft shortage; to order more planes: Piyush Goyal
text: Piyush Goyal has revealed plans to purchase an additional 1,000 civilian aircraft to tackle the pressing demand for air travel. This initiative comes as Indian airlines such as IndiGo and Air India have already placed sizable orders with leading manufacturers. In addition, there are ongoing efforts to improve air connectivity to Egypt and to forge partnerships with international aerospace companies to boost local aircraft production.

title: IDBI Bank employee unions call nationwide strike on Dec 3 against proposed stake sale
text: IDBI Bank employee unions have announced a one-day nationwide strike on December 3 to protest against the planned sale of the bank to Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings. The unions demand the government halt the sale, describing IDBI Bank as a national asset, while the Opposition raises concerns about the valuation and implications of the disinvestment.

title: Adani Green says Tarali Project has no protected area or forest land overlap
text: In a statement, Adani Green Energy Ltd (AGEL) said the 1,500-MW project in Maharashtra had secured the requisite statutory approvals before construction began. The company said it had received a no-forest-land certificate on January 23, 2024, and obtained the necessary land-use permissions and statutory no-objection certificates from the competent authorities.

title: Enhancing electrification can reduce India's energy import bill by over 40 pc by FY2035: Report
text: Accelerating electrification would reduce India's expenditure on import of crude oil, natural gas and coal to Rs 7.4 lakh crore by FY2035 from an estimated Rs 12.5 lakh crore in FY2025. On the current trajectory, however, it would rise to Rs 17 lakh crore.

title: SIFs emerge as the new heroes in a volatile market
text: The rise of Specialized Investment Funds (SIFs) marks a significant trend in investment circles, celebrated for their flexibility and diminished risk of loss. Functioning as an intermediary between Mutual Funds and Portfolio Management Services, SIFs accommodate various investment approaches. Their asset management has soared beyond ₹38,000 crore, signaling robust expansion since inception. Investors can opt for equity, bond, or hybrid SIFs to align with their risk tolerance.

title: Adani starts production of India's longest wind turbine blades
text: Adani New Industries Ltd has started manufacturing 91.2-metre wind turbine blades at its Mundra facility in Gujarat. This marks a significant advancement in India's capability for onshore wind energy production. The MWL185-5.0 MW platform has received certification from WindGuard Certification GmbH to proceed with serial production. Furthermore, Adani Wind aims to expand its manufacturing capacity beyond the current 2.25 GW state.

title: InGovern questions Zee's Rs 600 crore buyback, company says warrant funds intact
text: InGovern raised concerns about Zee Entertainment Enterprises Ltd's planned Rs 600-crore share buyback and its capital allocation strategy. The advisory firm noted the recent fundraising and questioned the need for returning capital to shareholders. Zee Entertainment defended its buyback, stating it reflects confidence in its growth prospects. The company emphasized its commitment to shareholder value and responsible capital allocation.

title: FSSAI scrutinises Red Bull's sugar levels as 'energy drink' dispute escalates
text: India is investigating the nutritional composition of Red Bull due to health concerns over added sugar. The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India warns that the energy drink label could mislead consumers. Red Bull has been given seven days to justify its labeling after receiving a notice from the FSSAI. Legal challenges have arisen from Red Bull and its competitors regarding regulatory actions.

title: RBI cancels registrations of 49 NBFCs; 13 NBFCs and one HFC surrender licenses
text: The Reserve Bank of India has revoked the registrations of 49 non-banking financial companies. Additionally, 13 companies, alongside a housing finance firm, voluntarily surrendered their registrations. This action reflects the RBI's commitment to maintaining oversight on financial institutions. Companies classified as unregistered Type I NBFCs or that halted operations will no longer participate in non-banking financial services.

title: Kalpataru Projects bags Rs 2,610 crore order in South America
text: Kalpataru Projects International has announced a significant order worth Rs 2,610 crore in South America. This order pertains to the company's power transmission lines and substations business sector. The company continues to witness strong order inflows, accumulating over Rs 26,000 crore in FY27. Furthermore, KPIL is well-positioned for additional projects amounting to approximately Rs 3,000 crore.

title: Tata Steel expects stronger performance in second half of fiscal: Narendran
text: Tata Steel anticipates improved performance in the second half of the fiscal year due to strong demand. The company is expanding its steel production capacity while exploring new plant locations in India. Operational challenges were faced earlier, but stabilisation is expected moving forward. The geopolitical situation remains a significant concern impacting operations. A gathering of tribal communities will take place, promoting cultural exchange and dialogue.

title: Biocon gets USFDA nod for breast cancer biosimilar Pebrilzo
text: Biocon Ltd has announced receiving US FDA approval for their biosimilar Pebrilzo, which treats HER2-positive breast cancer. This milestone adds to Biocon's portfolio, increasing their number of oncology biosimilars approved in the United States to five. The company has also secured a global settlement with Genentech for Pebrilzo's earliest licensed launch date in 2028.
